qs.q: A patient presents with a boggy, inflamed scalp lesion after a tinea capitis infection. Which immune response is primarily responsible for the lesion’s appearance?
qs.e: The lesion is a kerion, a Type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction to the dermatophyte.
qs.s: Mycoses: Fungal Pathogenesis, Virulence & Host Immune Defense: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following statements regarding Tinea nigra is NOT correct?
o: It causes hyperpigmented macules on the palms and soles.
The causative agent is typically Hortaea werneckii.
It is a systemic fungal infection requiring intravenous therapy.
It is a superficial fungal infection.
qs.e: Tinea nigra is a superficial fungal infection characterized by hyperpigmented macules on the palms and soles, caused by Hortaea werneckii. It is treated with topical antifungal agents, not intravenous therapy.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - October 9, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which of the following is a common cause of superficial skin infection characterized by hypopigmented or hyperpigmented patches, often referred to as 'sun spots' or 'tinea versicolor'?
qs.e: Malassezia globosa (and other Malassezia species) are the causative agents of pityriasis (tinea) versicolor, a superficial mycosis characterized by discolored skin patches, particularly on the trunk and shoulders.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: 26-year-old man, itchy white flaky stinging patches between toe webs/soles, inflammation, fissures. Likely agent: T. rubrum is the most common cause of chronic interdigital tinea pedis. ---
qs.e: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common cause of chronic interdigital tinea pedis.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases

qs.q: Fungal disease causing a blister-like lesion on the scalp: Dermatophyte infection of the scalp (tinea capitis) can present with vesicular/blister-like lesions. ---
qs.e: Dermatophytosis, specifically tinea capitis, can present with vesicular or blister-like lesions on the scalp.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases

qs.q: Immunocompromised persons and fungal disease — least frequently associated: Malassezia causes superficial disease (tinea versicolor), not typically severe disease in immunocompromised hosts. ---
qs.e: Malassezia causes superficial infections and is not typically associated with severe disease in immunocompromised hosts.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases

qs.q: All are superficial mycoses EXCEPT: Tinea imbricata is a cutaneous (not purely superficial) dermatophytosis. ---
qs.e: Tinea imbricata is classified as a cutaneous dermatophytosis rather than a strictly superficial mycosis.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases

qs.q: All are examples of superficial mycoses EXCEPT: Tinea pedis is a cutaneous dermatophytosis, invading keratin of skin — deeper than the truly superficial (stratum corneum surface only) infections. ---
qs.e: Tinea pedis is a cutaneous dermatophytosis extending deeper than true superficial mycoses limited to the stratum corneum.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases
